title: Egg Drop: Fewest Moves
src: Media.net OA, IIT Patna (reported alongside the set above, from a screenshot).
body:
You have A identical eggs and a building with floors 1 to B. There is an unknown floor C (0 ≤ C ≤ B): an egg dropped from a floor above C breaks, and an egg dropped from floor C or below survives and can be dropped again. A broken egg can't be reused.

Each move drops one unbroken egg from a floor of your choice. Return the minimum number of moves that guarantees you find C, whatever its value.

Function to complete

Complete superEggDrop(A, B). It returns the minimum number of moves.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
out: One integer: the minimum number of moves in the worst case.

wrong.why: binary search: ignores how many eggs there are
off by one: needs f[A] ≥ B + 1

samples.ex: With one egg you must try floor 1, then floor 2: 2 moves.
Drop from floor 3. If it breaks, try floors 1 and 2 with the last egg. If not, floor 5, then 4 or 6. 3 moves always suffice.
